newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum - Not right to say German mkts are rigid.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum - Not right to say German mkts are rigid.

text.p: Bundesbank deputy president Johann Gaddum said on Tuesday that were now no grounds on which to accuse Germany of having rigid financial markets.

Speaking at a news conference, Gaddum said the government and the Bundesbank were looking at ways to modernise the process of issuing sovereign debt, adding that he thought all market players should have the chance to participate in the issue of government debt.

Bonn's debt is currently sold by the Bundesbank through a consortium of banks, which then sell it on the the market. The system has been criticised by some market participants who say it favours the banks in the consortium.
The Bundesbank said earlier that it had sold 3.0 billion marks of the government's new 30-year strippable bond at a price of 99.75 to the consortium.
Gaddum also told the news conference that he did not expect to see any negative impact on the bond markets from the new 30-year paper.
